steps: Navigated to http://127.0.0.1:8080/ on a fresh backend
Read the accessibility snapshot
Checked the body of the GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/counter response
Later, in a second pass, reloaded the page and took the screenshot evidence/ac1-initial.png
criteria.observed: The page shows an h1 heading 'Counter', a paragraph with the number '0' and a button 'Increment'. The GET /counter response body was {"value":0}. In the second pass (backend at 4), the page showed '4', matching GET /counter. Note: my first round of screenshots used relative filenames and were saved outside evidence/, probably in the Playwright working directory (the frontend scratchpad). I retook all evidence into evidence/.

steps: Clicked 'Increment' once
Read the snapshot and the network log
Read the POST response body
Repeated in a second pass with a screenshot
criteria.observed: One click produced exactly one POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/counter/increment (200) with body {"value":1}. The number changed from 0 to 1. In the second pass it went from 4 to 5, with response {"value":5}, and exactly one POST was sent.

steps: Clicked 'Increment' three times, waiting for the number to update after each click
Took a screenshot
Reloaded the page
Checked that GET /counter was sent again and read its response
Took a screenshot
criteria.observed: The number went 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 (up by 3), each value matching its POST response. After the reload, a new GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/counter returned {"value":8} and the page showed 8. The first pass behaved the same way: 1 → 4, then 4 after reload.

steps: Read the full browser network log (static resources included) after every phase of testing
criteria.observed: Every backend request was GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/counter or POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/counter/increment. All other requests were static assets from the frontend origin 127.0.0.1:8080 (/, styles.css, config.js, app.js, api.js). No other backend endpoint was requested.

steps: Used Playwright page.route in the browser to abort every request to http://127.0.0.1:3000/** with connectionrefused
Clicked 'Increment' and read the page text
Took a screenshot
Reloaded the page with the backend still blocked and read the page text
Took a screenshot
Removed the route
criteria.observed: When Increment was clicked, the page kept '8' and showed a visible message: 'Could not increment the counter: Could not reach the backend (Failed to fetch).' When the page loaded, the number showed '—' and a visible message: 'Could not load the counter: Could not reach the backend (Failed to fetch).' I simulated the unreachable backend by aborting its requests in the browser; the real backend process was not stopped.
